title: Loot is a loan until you extract.
author: OwnStatistician2868
selftext:
The run back was the whole point. Find a Golden Eagle in Kessel, get your squad moving, and suddenly that bag matters more than the next fight. You only keep what you get out with. Die, and the haul is gone.



That became Extract or Die. I built it on Spawn by talking with Savi. I was using AI, but I was deciding what the game should be, checking what was on screen and pushing back when it missed.



First, I gave it a direction:



"art direction for everything new: realistic proportions, mid-poly, real-world materials, muted colors, nothing blocky or cartoony, light enough to run well."



I wanted a soldier who looked like he belonged there. Start in the bunker, go through the Blast Door into Kessel. Come back with loot, or lose the gear he left with.



A friend and I managed to stand at the same Blast Door in two different games. We could not see each other. I added a ready-up at the door. Going through together needed to actually mean together.



Then there was the rifle. Crouch and aim, and it went up over his head. I kept explaining where the barrel should point, where the stock should sit, what his hands should be doing.



"I don't know what I have to tell you to make you fix the crouching aim"



The tester pictures did not match what I could see on my own character. A fix had to survive the way I actually played, not just look right in a still.



Eventually I could type:



"crouch + aim is fixed, I tested it, thanks."



Then moving while crouched sent it overhead again. So that became the next thing to fight through, until:



"its looking better no flailing so far good job"



That was the victory I wanted from the build. A soldier holding his rifle properly while I moved him.



I also had two solo raiders go through the Blast Door separately. They landed in the same raid as enemies. I had them shoot each other to prove it. Getting players into the same city mattered as much as making the soldier behave.



After 85.9 hours from my first message, I made the call:



"Let's publish this."



Now the argument belongs to the players. One more crate, or extraction? I built the city. You decide how much you dare carry.
